description: The new Sioux Falls mayor, who received endorsements from the two remaining GOP Gubernatorial candidates in a runoff, is endorsing the incumbent governor.

description: Badlands is the first and only park in South Dakota to be designated as an International Dark Sky Park.

description: Rural economies offer unique challenges no matter where they are. In Eagle Butte though, a reservation community in central South Dakota, steps are being taken for a diversified, localized economy that are already visible on Main Street.

description: A research team at Dakota State University is surveying and identifying microplastics in the state's bodies of water. We explore the state's first comprehensive search for microplastics.

description: The "Tremors & Soar" showcase highlights the artistry of the LiRa Dance Theatre Company. Co-founders Lisa Conlin and Raena Rasmussen talk about the art and business of dance.

Doeden goes back to business; Rhoden cites 
'walking by faith.' Here are the candidate speeches from election night
byline: By Lori Walsh, Jackson Dircks, Jackie Hendry
description: Gov. Larry Rhoden bested Aberdeen businessman Toby Doeden in a Republican runoff election. Rhoden will face Democrat Dan Ahlers in November. But first, both candidates thanked their supporters in election night speeches.

byline: By Jackie Hendry, Jackson Dircks, Josh Chilson
description: Gov. Larry Rhoden is set to represent the Republican Party in the race South Dakota governor this November.

description: Gov. Larry Rhoden was not your typical incumbent. Yet he used his office to reset relationships and convince Republican primary voters he was the right candidate to carry the GOP banner in November. Seth Tupper offers analysis into Rhoden's win.

title: Tribe receives $1.4M grant to establish recycling, composting program

description: Larry Rhoden has won the Republican gubernatorial runoff, after a hard-fought primary cycle. If elected in November, he would be the first governor in recent history to be voted in from West River.

description: What would you say if your child was given a savings account to help with college at five years old? For some families in the Black Hills, that’s becoming a reality.

description: Lake Area Technical College in Watertown is adding a radiology technician program. That’s following approval from a state board.

description: As Pennington County reels from what it describes as a cybersecurity “incident,” Rapid City has also become a victim.

description: The homeowners involved in the Hideaway Hills subdivision sinkhole case are requesting a rehearing after the after the South Dakota Supreme Court ruled against them.

description: From a massive balance sheet to the way the Fed communicates, Fed Chair's Kevin Warsh's new task forces will take a comprehensive look at U.S. monetary policy. Macroeconomist Joe Santos weighs in on the complicated work of reform now before the Fed.

description: The development of a new Rapid City business and industrial park is receiving state backing. Gov. Larry Rhoden announces a $1 million investment from the Future Fund.

description: Rapid City and communities in the Pactola/Rapid Creek watershed should have enough water to last nearly the next century. However, that’s only if managed and utilized properly.

description: President Trump's executive order about a U.S. Postal Service rule is before the U.S. Supreme Court. How much can a president weigh in on how elections are conducted?

description: One South Dakota-based group is urging Congress against delaying federal THC regulations passed last year and set to take effect this fall.

description: Bikers are revving up for the Sturgis Rally, but it comes at a complicated time. With the increased traffic, the rally annually brings a corresponding rise in crashes, some of which result in serious injuries. This year, the event is taking place at the same time as a nationwide blood shortage.

Now the other side of the aisle is trying to make up ground. For “Dakota Democrats” the focus is listening and localizing.

description: A South Dakota Democrat vying for statewide office says he’s receiving bipartisan support following the GOP nomination.

description: South Dakota’s farmers and ranchers have been dealing with impacts of tariffs, the war in Iran and environmental factors as they try to turn a profit.

description: Four new programs ranging from bachelor’s to doctoral degrees in AI-focused fields are coming to Dakota State and South Dakota State Universities.

description: As state Democrats try to build momentum during the summer political doldrums, Murdoc (Brad Jurgenson) has thoughts on where they might put their focus for maximum results.

description: Over two decades after the fact, the state has dismissed charges against two men connected to the presumed death of Beverly Ann Ozuna-Ulrich.

description: The Dahl Arts Center in Rapid City is home to not only the visual arts, but also the performing arts. Twice monthly, new and old voices can be heard working on their craft in the space.

description: Jazz vocalist and bandleader Alyssa Allgood stops by the SDPB studios alongside Jim Spiers and Daniel Heier. The trio talks jazz, community, and creative practice.

description: South Dakota’s senator and the U.S. Senate Republican Majority Leader said elections are “breaking [Republicans'] way” ahead of Midterm elections. Though, it’s not without challenges for the party.

title: SE Tech hopes new $18 million facility meets skilled manufacturing demands
description: Southeast Technical College broke ground on a project the school hopes meets the demand for skilled manufacturing professionals in the state.

description: South Dakota State University is collaborating on a research project that could potentially change the future of organ transplantations.

description: These two circuits are the Fourth and Seventh, which would create by far the largest judicial district in the state by area.

description: One of South Dakota’s U.S. senators introduces a bill incentivizing ranchers to convert cropland back to grassland. Though, the land could still be grazed and hayed under emergency conditions. The bill is in response to the smallest U.S. cow herd size in multiple decades.

description: State tribal leaders say there is a disconnect between services promised to tribal nations and those provided. Right now, they say that discrepancy is highlighted in law enforcement.

description: Both of South Dakota’s most prominent airports are requesting more funds for expansion projects. Rapid City and Sioux Falls Regional leadership say construction is the path forward to keeping terminals up to standard.

description: South Dakota is a state looking to strengthen its reach on the international trade market. Representatives of other nations the state is looking to grow partnerships with tell SDPB they see opportunities.

description: A major regional energy utility is seeking a rate increase to pay for a new electricity powerplant in Rapid City.

description: A Pierre woman convicted of defrauding the state’s Medicaid program has avoided a jail sentence for the crime.

description: The state faces a lawsuit over its implementation of a voting law. The question arises not from the law itself, but the administration of that law which critics say creates confusion ahead of election season.

description: A recent survey showed businesses across the region are facing high costs and struggling with passing those costs on to consumers.

description: President Donald Trump is endorsing Republican incumbent Larry Rhoden in the race for South Dakota governor.

description: A party in Perkins County explores reciprocal relationships and how to be part of a nation of gatherers. We talk with Eliza Blue and Garrett Bucks.

description: "We're all doing great ... and other lies" showcases standup comedy that intersects with addiction recovery. Producer Joe Huisman talks about laughing together through pain and chaos.

description: President Donald Trump is endorsing Republican incumbent Larry Rhoden in the race for South Dakota governor.

description: South Dakota has submitted a waiver to exclude soda-like drinks from federal program recipients in the state. However, it comes with both immediate and ongoing costs.

description: Authorities say South Dakota law enforcement have made an arrest in a child abduction case out of Wyoming.

description: A woman with decades of experience in the justice system is set to serve as South Dakota's Missing and Murdered Indigenous Person specialist.

description: September marks Hunger Action Month, and that’s even more important in a state with significant food insecurity. According to Feeding South Dakota, one in five of the state’s children face food insecurity.

description: Applications are now open for South Dakota’s free or reduced-price meals for eligible families for the 2026-27 school year.
